title: Omniscient Author's Viewpoint
html:
“I'm an author.”

When she had only recently begun writing, Han Sooyoung used to introduce herself that way.

She had done it on a blind date she attended at a friend's earnest insistence, too.

“Oh, you're an author!”

What a fuss. He must have heard that before coming.

The man's eyes darted about before he smiled and asked,

“Then did you make your literary debut through one of those New Year's writing contests?”

“No.”

“Huh? Then···.”

“I write webnovels.”

“Webnovels?”

This was always where the trouble began.

She could see his eyes sweep over her shabby hoodie.

“Aha, so··· you mean those? Internet novels? The ones with all the emoticons···?”

“Ah, yeees. Those would be the ones.”

“There are so many unusual jobs these days. YouTubers, internet writers···.”

The man smiled and took a long sip of the Americano in front of him. A glance at his watch revealed a fairly expensive brand.

···This was a scene she'd seen plenty of times before.

“Everyone seems to want easy money these days. Don't you think?”

“Does anyone want to earn money the hard way?”

“I make about a hundred million won a year myself, and it's no easy feat. That's why people like that make me sigh. Trying to get other people's money without working for it···.”

From the way he spoke, he seemed to have forgotten this was supposed to be a blind date. Looking slightly annoyed, he glanced at the car key on the table. For someone his age, it was quite an expensive imported car.

Letting his words go in one ear and out the other, Han Sooyoung switched on her smartphone. A host of new comment notifications had appeared.

—Author-nim, isn't this getting way too frustrating?

—Hmm... The next chapter starts with some satisfying payoff, right? Otherwise, I'm dropping this.

“People who never studied hard when they were young get lucky and···.”

Suddenly, she thought she understood why people read webnovels.

She also understood why her bastard of a friend had introduced her to this nobody. Her friend had said she would understand when they met. Now it was perfectly clear what they had hoped for when sending her here.

Normally, she would have let it pass because dealing with it was a bother, but···.

“So··· are you listening?”

“Ah, yes. Your salary was···?”

Only then did his eyes light up. His shoulders straightened, as though he had known she would ask him that again.

“A hundred million won after tax.”

“Hmm. About the same as me.”

“Pardon?”

The man snorted.

“You earn a hundred million a year as a writer?”

Han Sooyoung shrugged and took a car key out of her pocket. A brand-new Porsche, the latest model. It cost exactly three times as much as his car. She hardly even drove it, since that was a bother, too.

His eyes wavered with the swaying key. Then an awkward smile appeared.

“Haha, but··· writers have irregular incomes, so they don't really have an ‘annual salary,’ do they? Your earnings aren't consistent, after all.”

His chattering lips reeled off one predictable remark after another. Just right for the lines of a villain who would make a brief appearance in the next installment. Then the protagonist could say this.

“I never said anything about a year.”

“Pardon? Oh, then that's everything you've earned in your life?”

“I've made a hundred million so far this month, and, hmm··· it's only mid-month, with two weeks still to go···.”

“···What?”

Only then, as though something had dawned on him, did the man's face begin to turn rapidly pale.

In the end, it had worked out just as her friend wanted.

Written into a novel, this would have been a satisfying payoff. In reality, it didn't feel all that good.

The man was frantically messaging someone. Probably asking the friend who had arranged the date a barrage of questions.

“Um, what was the title of your novel···?”

Just as she was thinking she didn't want to tell this guy the title,

another notification appeared on Han Sooyoung's smartphone.

—Hello, author-nim. I'm a reader who enjoys webnovels. I happened to read your work···.

What was this long message? She tapped the notification without thinking. The language was polite and old-fashioned, with even a touch of earnest innocence.

—Your work bears far too great a resemblance to a novel I love, ‘Three Ways to Survive in a Ruined World.’

···Who the hell was this?

「That was Han Sooyoung and Kim Dokja's first meeting.」

Kim Dokja.

「Watching the scene unfold before her, Han Sooyoung recalled that memory.」

She had lost some of her memories while making avatars, so the events of that time did not come back clearly. But one thing was certain. She had, at the time, read the novel called ‘Ways of Survival.’

Because of none other than the guy with the username ‘Kim Dokja.’

—Author-nim! Today's chapter was so much fun, too.

At Han Sooyoung's level, a few chapters were enough to tell whether a work would become a hit.

But to her eye, ‘Ways of Survival’ would never become a hit—not in this life or the next.

—This is a really interesting beginning.

It was boring as fuck from the very start.

—Author-nim, does that mean Yoo Joonghyuk remembers all of that? Then in the 72nd round···.

It was far too expository.

—Ahh, so close! Joonghyuk will get his act together next round, right? Today's chapter was a blast, too.

The protagonist was a personality-free male lead who did nothing but look handsome and mow down his enemies. And on top of that,

—Author-nim! Congratulations on reaching 2,000 chapters! Since you've come this far, I hope you'll write another thousand···.

There were far too many chapters, too.

‘···He thinks this is fun? Is he out of his mind?’

Sometimes she got so annoyed that she went through his comments and downvoted them.

As though bewitched, Han Sooyoung was avidly reading Kim Dokja's comments rather than the novel.

—Does Jihye finally awaken in the next chapter?

—Author-nim! I found a typo on page seven! In my humble opinion, the spelling here··· Ah, I looked it up and I was wrong. Sorry. I learned something today.

—Please smack that bastard Joonghyuk in the back of the head···.

Comments on thousands of chapters, without a single one missed. Every one of them held understanding and affection for the world the author had created.

「Han Sooyoung envied that.」

She thought there could be no such reader for a novel this lousy. Of course it had to be the author doing it. She imagined the writer had made two accounts to write the novel, comment on it, and even post recommendations.

—I believe recommending your own work is against the rules?

「Just as Yoo Joonghyuk was fictional to Kim Dokja, Kim Dokja was fictional to Han Sooyoung.」

She hadn't thought such a person could exist.

And now that person from the text was before her eyes.

“Dokja-ssi—!”

A high ringing in her ears. Explosions erupting everywhere.

At the center of the battlefield raging like a storm, Han Sooyoung watched Kim Dokja fight through the torrent of stars. Incarnations screamed, stars roared. The dokkaebis in the air were laughing.

【■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■】

Kim Dokja was shouting. Whether it was a scream, a proclamation, or a cry of anguish, Han Sooyoung couldn't hear it. Now that he had become an Outer God, his voice was utterly excluded from the scenario. Whatever he said, its meaning no longer mattered.

Gyaaaaaaaaaah!

But there were Outer Gods who followed him. Remnants abandoned across countless worldlines were gathering at Kim Dokja's side. In the sky of the final scenario, Myth-grade constellations awaited him.

[It has finally begun.]

Zeus, the ‘Lightning Throne,’ king of <Olympus> and ruler of the Twelve Divine Seats, was there.

[The worldline's ‘final scenario’ has begun!]

[All beings in the final scenario have acquired the right to participate!]

[Kill Kim Dokja, the ‘Enemy of the Story.’]

Scenario messages appeared one after another. Everyone there understood the situation.

Zeus was the first to speak.

[Wipe them out.]

With a sound that seemed to bring down the heavens, Zeus's lightning poured down. Something burst with a wet pop, and blood splashed onto Han Sooyoung's cheek. Nameless Ones were dying, spraying black blood.

【Helphelphelphelphe···.】

Even the terrifying ‘Outer Gods’ were no more than water balloons before the combined Status of the Myth-grade constellations. Mercilessly blown apart, the ‘Outer Gods’ retched out discarded Stories.

Dazzling lightning. At the center of the ruins, Kim Dokja was enduring Zeus's electric assault.

Why had Kim Dokja made that choice?

[Tear his wings! Seal off the area!]

With the constellations' roars, an immense army of stars swept in. Constellations and incarnations who had survived hellish scenarios to reach this place were surging forward as one, intent only on eliminating ‘Kim Dokja.’

What saved him was the Great Sage, Heaven's Equal, who had become one with him.

[The constellation, ‘Most Ancient Liberator,’ reveals his Status!]

Lightning flowing proudly across the sky. The lightning of the Great Sage, Heaven's Equal, drove back Zeus's and tore the heavens apart like a drumskin.

The constellations faltered for an instant before shouts of encouragement rang out.

[It's the Great Sage, Heaven's Equal!]

[Don't retreat! Once he dies, the scenario ends!]

[This is the last scenario of this worldline!]

The hope that, at last, they could be freed from everything.

Among them were constellations and incarnations whose faces she had glimpsed in passing.

“No need to feel guilty! He chose this himself!”

<Olympus>, <Vedas>, <Papyrus>, <Guardian Tree>, <Twelve Zodiacs>, <Emperor>···.

Constellations and incarnations from nebulas most people had heard of at least once were there.

There was no one there who didn't know who Kim Dokja was.

「Every one of them raised a sword to kill Kim Dokja.」

A white coat showed through a torn black coat. Kim Dokja was there, cast in a role that did not suit him.

Kim Dokja, in tatters, spreading torn black and white wings, with demon king horns on his head.

Kim Dokja, swinging his sword at the enemy from the vanguard of the Outer Gods.

For a moment, her vision seemed to blur white. Then Kim Dokja's figure began to fade.

The alien eyes peculiar to a cephalopod. A clammy outer hide.

Where Kim Dokja had been stood a vast Outer God King, as though every grotesque creature in the world had been mixed together.

「Enemy of the Story」

As an author, Han Sooyoung knew instinctively.

If this world were a novel, Kim Dokja was now the ‘final boss.’

And this story would only end when that ‘Kim Dokja’ died.

“Han Sooyoung!”

Someone pulled her away. A torrent of lightning swept past the tip of her nose.

“Get back! Hurry!”

It was Yoo Sangah. She alone had kept her head in this frenzied chaos. How could she?

“Everyone, get a grip! Right now, Dokja-ssi is···!”

Kim Dokja would die.

“We made a promise to Dokja-ssi! Have you all forgotten?”

Kim Dokja was a liar.

“There's no way Dokja-ssi would really do the same thing again···!”

Someone who believed in people's goodwill. That was Yoo Sangah. Because she was Yoo Sangah, because she trusted people more than anyone, she could remain unshaken even now. That was why she and Han Sooyoung had always clashed.

Despite Yoo Sangah's cries, their companions' faces were blank. With unfocused eyes, each was lost in thought. The question holding them captive was the same.

「Why on earth had Kim Dokja made that choice?」

He had promised. He had sworn never to sacrifice himself like that again.

「Why?」

“The story isn't over yet.”

Yoo Sangah was wrong. The story's direction was already decided. Kim Dokja had become the ‘Enemy of the Story,’ and this goddamn scenario would only end when he died.

The author who had written all this tragedy had already decided it.

···The author?

【■■■■■■■■■■!】

Kim Dokja's voice rang out in anguish. That voice returned as a memory from some time ago.

—Han Sooyoung, you're an author, right?

Han Sooyoung's mind raced.

—What are you picking a fight over now?

—There's something I want to ask.

—What?

—Is an author really all-powerful and all-knowing within what they write?

—What the hell brought that on?

—No, I'm just curious. Do you control everything when you write? This character moves like this, that character acts like that···.

—Well, of course···.

With perfect confidence, Han Sooyoung declared,

—I can't.

—Why not? You're the author.

—Do you think authors are actually gods?

—The author makes everything in a story, though. The situations, the characters···.

You have no idea what you're talking about, Han Sooyoung muttered.

—Characters start doing whatever they want the moment you create them. The author only sets the stage. The characters are the ones who choose how to react to events and what to do.

—You mean that literally, not as a metaphor?

—Literally.

—You sure have an easy time writing.

—You wanna die?

Kim Dokja, doubling over after a blow to the stomach.

What had he been thinking then?

—That's interesting. Even the author isn't the god of the story···. Then who exactly gets to decide a ‘scenario’?

A chill slowly rose from her toes. Perhaps the Kim Dokja over there was an answer to that question.

Tsu-tsu-tsu-tsuch!

Perhaps Kim Dokja had thought of it.

The only way to change the ending in this unyielding world of scenarios.

[The Great Dokkaebis are flustered by the flood of probability!]

[<Star Stream> watches the shifting course of probability!]

Scenarios were not perfect.

[The ‘final scenario’ is undergoing a radical upheaval!]

The author was certainly the one who made a story.

But the characters were the ones who lived it.

And the ones who decided their fate were—

[The constellations of the Korean Peninsula cheer for ‘Demon King of Salvation’!]

[The constellations of <Eden> cheer for ‘Demon King of Salvation’!]

[The constellations of the <Underworld> cheer for ‘Demon King of Salvation’!]

[The constellations of an unknown planet cheer for ‘Demon King of Salvation’!]

[Countless constellations donate coins!]

[The overwhelming majority of constellations watch the final fight of ‘Demon King of Salvation’!]

The people watching that story.

Tsu-tsu-tsu-tsuch!

[Many constellations do not want ‘Demon King of Salvation’ to die!]

The only beings who could change a ‘scenario.’

Kim Dokja had not become the ‘Enemy of the Story’ in order to die here.

He had not chosen sacrifice in order to betray his companions.

「‘Ways of Survival’ was Yoo Joonghyuk's story. Then whose story was this world now?」

Watching the world's probability waver, Han Sooyoung muttered bitterly.

“···Right. No reader wants the protagonist to die.”

In this world, the influence of Kim Dokja and <Kim Dokja’s Company> had grown immense.

His becoming the target of the final scenario was proof of that.

Whether they liked it or not, the constellations had seen Kim Dokja's Stories and had empathized with them or felt jealous. Whether he wanted them to or not, all the stars in this world were now watching his story. Kim Dokja probably knew it, too.

Perhaps he had been thinking about it for a very long time.

「This was the final gamble of Kim Dokja, who had become a ‘character.’」

She felt as though Kim Dokja had turned to look at her from afar.

As though to say that she would understand this.

As though to say that from here, they could begin a new story they knew nothing about.

「He had sacrificed himself in order not to sacrifice himself.」

It might be impossible. It might be an ending they could never reach.

But it was the only ‘way for no one to be sacrificed’ that Kim Dokja had found.

So what Han Sooyoung could do now was clear.

‘He can't do this alone.’

Han Sooyoung turned around. She had to tell their companions what Kim Dokja wanted now.

But there was something Han Sooyoung, elated by her own understanding, had not realized.

[The Story, ‘Predictive Plagiarism,’ predicts the characters' states of mind.]

Not everyone here was an author.

Not everyone could view this situation so objectively.

Before Han Sooyoung could open her mouth, one of their companions darted forward.

Fierce hostility in a sword stroke.

The instant she saw where the sword's point was heading, Han Sooyoung recoiled in horror.

“Wait! Hold on! Right now, he's—”

She couldn't believe it, because she knew whose sword it was.

「Someone who had come to resent Kim Dokja very deeply at this moment.」

Kim Dokja's sturdiest sword, which had protected him for so long.

That sword moved to end this scenario.

[Your ■■ is ■■.]

When Jung Heewon first heard that message, she had felt uneasy. Something Kim Dokja once said had come to mind. Every being had a different final curtain. She had thought she would have one, too.

But······ ■■?

Jung Heewon knew someone that word suited far better.

Someone who had fought closer to her than anyone.

Someone whose sword she could become without hesitation.

Someone who treasured his companions. Someone who always sacrificed himself first.

「Someone she therefore could not help resenting.」

Jung Heewon ran through the waves of ‘Nameless Ones.’ Poison splashing from nearby soaked her shin, and her flesh swelled black. She hastily took out the wound ointment Lee Seolhwa had given her, applied it, and ran again. Shaking off the constellations' attacks from either side, she trampled over the Nameless Ones gathered around Kim Dokja like guards and leaped up.

She saw something in the distance.

Something that had once been ‘Kim Dokja.’

【■■■■■!】

And had now become the 「Enemy of the Story」.

“Heewon-ssi!”

Lee Hyunsung, who had barely managed to catch up, grabbed Jung Heewon's shoulder.

“Wait—”

Before he could finish, a message appeared.

[Streaming of the final scenario to all regions begins!]

Every channel in <Star Stream> was opening.

Tsu-tsuch, tsu-tsu-tsuch······!

Scenario messages flickering unsteadily.

[Please remain calm and concentrate on the scenario. This is your final scenario. Once you hunt down the Outer God King, your long journey will end.]

[This story will be recorded on the ‘Final Wall,’ and the journey of the stars will remain an ‘epic,’ passed down for eternity!]

The Great Dokkaebis, crying out greedily.

Their eyes shone with the desire to leave the Stories they had guided upon the Final Wall.

[The Giant Story, ‘Radiance of the Aged Dawn,’ dreams of the final story!]

[The Giant Story, ‘Master of Asgard,’ dreams of the final story!]

The Giant Stories were stirring, too.

To remain as ‘A Single Story,’ they urged on the constellations and incarnations.

[The constellation, ‘Spear that Parts the Boundaries of the Sea,’ takes out his weapon!]

[The constellation, ‘Master of Abydos,’ descends into the scenario!]

[The constellation, ‘Mysterious Bird of the Nile,’ lets out a fierce roar!]

But not everyone was swept along by that encouragement.

Despite the orders of Zeus, the First Divine Seat, several deities of <Olympus>, including Dionysus, hesitated to attack. So did some incarnations.

“······Do we really, really have to kill him?”

It was the Japanese incarnation ‘Asuka Ren’ who spoke.

“The ‘Kim Dokja’ I saw wasn't an evil person.”

“That's right! Kim Dogeza isn't a bad person!”

People who had fought against the other Japanese who chose to become disasters during [Peace Land], and had received help from Kim Dokja and his companions.

Several incarnations belonging to <Emperor> and <Olympus> agreed, too.

[A considerable number of constellations agree with the incarnations!]

[The probability of <Star Stream> wavers!]

Sensing an unusual turn in probability, the Great Dokkaebis stepped forward again.

[Do not forget. He is the ‘enemy of the scenario.’]

[You may not know this, but ‘Kim Dokja’ has been clearing scenarios from the very beginning in order to ruin this worldline.]

Unlike their usual manner, those arrogant Great Dokkaebis began their narration in polite tones.

Images of Stories were projected across the vast sky. The dokkaebis' specialty had begun.

[He betrayed this worldline and made deals with the ‘Outer Gods.’]

On the screen, Kim Dokja was making a deal with ‘Secretive Plotter.’ Without their voices, his expression looked all the more sinister.

And that was not all. Everything Kim Dokja had done until now was being laid bare for all to see.

How he had released grasshoppers on the subway instead of saving people.

How he had left people at Geumho Station to their fate when he could have saved more······.

A collection of only someone's worst moments was creating a new Kim Dokja for the world.

[If he achieves his aim, this world will only be destroyed.]

Soon, the screen switched to 「Journey to the West」.

The Giant Story, 「The Liberator of the Forgotten Ones」.

Surrounded by Outer Gods, Kim Dokja was freeing the ‘Nameless Ones’ trapped in the scenario.

But perhaps because of the dokkaebis' staging, the Kim Dokja in that Story no longer looked holy. He looked like the leader of a heretical cult, releasing demons to destroy this world.

[He acquired knowledge of the future by some means and used it for his own benefit.]

Holding a smartphone, Kim Dokja was giving his companions orders.

[His becoming ‘Demon King of Salvation’ and ‘Watcher of Light and Darkness’ alike. All of it was simply part of his plan.]

Working together, the storytellers were dragging Kim Dokja down from ‘protagonist’ to villain. They were making his Stories base and cowardly.

[The probability of <Star Stream> moves!]

It was clearly a violation of a storyteller's duty.

Even so, the Great Dokkaebis did not hesitate. Storytellers, too, had a ■■ they wanted.

[And now, as the monarch of the ‘Outer Gods,’ he is trying to destroy this world.]

Tsu-tsu-tsu-tsuch!

Public opinion in <Star Stream> was changing rapidly.

Anna Croft passed the pale Asuka Ren with an unreadable expression and murmured indifferently,

“It's already too late.]

The members of ‘Zarathustra’ began their charge, and the hesitating constellations joined the battle.

Gyaaaaaaaaaah!

The ‘Nameless Ones’ collided with the constellations' vanguard, screaming in pain.

「Everyone connected to Kim Dokja was pointing their swords at one another.」

And in the middle of that battlefield, Jung Heewon watched Kim Dokja fight.

Even without her help, there were many ‘Outer Gods’ fighting at his side. Huge cephalopod monsters. Outer Gods with babies' torsos and enormous flowers for heads.

Even if she borrowed Uriel's power and gave it everything she had, Jung Heewon could not be sure. Among them, Kim Dokja truly looked like a great calamity that would end this worldline.

「Jung Heewon had thought she understood Kim Dokja.」

She did not know what ending Kim Dokja truly wanted.

But she had thought she could tell without being told. That he wanted the same end of the world she did.

「But what if that was the ending he truly wanted?」

What if, to him, there had never been any companions at all?

[The constellation, ‘Demon-like Judge,’······!]

She knew. Jung Heewon knew better than anyone what Uriel wanted to say.

She knew Kim Dokja treasured his companions. Knew he had done this precisely because he treasured them so much.

He was probably planning to sacrifice his life to send his companions to the end of the world.

「No matter how far she reached, she could not grasp him.」

It was as though a vast wall stood before her.

As though that wall kept her from reaching Kim Dokja.

“Why······.”

Perhaps Jung Heewon was now too exhausted to keep longing for the ending she wanted.

「Kim Dokja was someone who could hear nothing.」

The sword's grip was cold as she slowly closed her hand around it. A sword Kim Dokja had made himself and placed in her hand. A sword that had been her conviction ever since [Paradise].

[The ‘Sword of Judgement’ cries out!]

The sword that cried only when ‘evil’ was near was weeping.

As though mocking her, the Great Dokkaebis declared,

[This is the unknown truth of ‘Kim Dokja,’ the Enemy of the Story.]

She wanted to make sure.

Whether you really are the ‘Kim Dokja’ I know.

And if what you want isn't what I want.

「Whether it would really be all right for me to end you with my own hands.」

“Heewon-ssi.”

As though he knew her thoughts, Lee Hyunsung was there.

“I'll go with you.”

Becoming a literal steel shield, Lee Hyunsung broke a path and ran.

They advanced through the waves of stars and the storm of Nameless Ones. Just as Jung Heewon had things she needed to confirm, Lee Hyunsung probably did, too.

Something he had to make certain of over and over, and then over and over again.

Kwa-kwa-kwa-kwa!

The two soared as though riding a wave, drawing close behind Kim Dokja in an instant.

It was only possible because all the other Outer Gods were concentrated at the front.

“Heewon-ssi!”

Was it because of the ring of Chaos drawn on the back of her hand? Even when the ‘Nameless Ones’ noticed her, they simply surged forward as though they had seen nothing.

Kim Dokja stood there, towering like an enormous building. A vast body dripping pitch-black slime.

Without realizing it, Jung Heewon reached out and touched that hide.

It was unfamiliar.

Once, she had firmly held the sleeping Kim Dokja's hand.

His hand, when he had come back as a returnee and spent the whole day unconscious in the room their companions had prepared.

What had that hand felt like?

As though sensing her, the Outer God King moved its enormous head and looked back.

Kugugugugu······.

White breath streaming from that enormous head.

“Kim Dok······.”

Though she knew she shouldn't, Jung Heewon stepped back despite herself.

An enormous maw was opening toward her.

[The scenario's probability moves!]

[All your Stories give a warning!]

Her reflection lay in the vast Outer God King's black eyes.

She hadn't wanted to make that face. Hadn't wanted to look at Kim Dokja with those eyes.

But her hand was already moving against her will.

“Aaaaaaaaah!”

The [Sword of Judgement] sliced through the approaching tentacles. As though facing an irreconcilable enemy, her sword moved wildly.

Stories spilled from the severed tentacles with a wet gush.

「“Dokja-ssi, you're happier now than you were back then, aren't you?”

“······If you're asking whether things are better now than they were then, yes.」

It was a Story she knew well, too.

「“Me too.”」

Staggering, she listened to that story. That story, remembered by no one in the world but Kim Dokja and Jung Heewon, steadied her mind.

As the haze cleared from her eyes, she saw the scene around her. She thought she had severed quite a few tentacles, yet there were no significant wounds. In the meantime, Kim Dokja had grown even larger. It was hard to believe this was just one person.

Kim Dokja was like a single, immense wall standing alone.

【■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■······】

A wall she could never fill, no matter what sentences she wrote upon it. Before that wall, Jung Heewon despaired.

What did the [Final Wall] matter? She could not even get past the wall of a single person.

In the distance, she saw Han Sooyoung approaching and shouting toward her.

Could Han Sooyoung get past this wall?

—Must be nice, being a writer.

A holiday for <Kim Dokja’s Company>.

Lying halfway up a mountain, Jung Heewon had said that to Han Sooyoung.

—Not really.

—No, why not? People who write well are good at expressing themselves clearly when they speak, too. I wish I could do that.

—Planning to write Lee Hyunsung a love letter?

—That's not what I mean.

Jung Heewon looked silently toward Kim Dokja. That glance alone seemed enough for Han Sooyoung to understand what she meant.

Kim Dokja, at a loss before his companions. Watching the man foolishly carry out a joke of a scenario called [Workers' Holiday], Han Sooyoung had said,

—Anyone can write.

Jung Heewon raised her head again and looked at what had once been Kim Dokja.

She was not an author like Han Sooyoung. Nor was she a diligent reader like Kim Dokja. She could neither write like Han Sooyoung nor read like Kim Dokja.

But that did not mean she could neither write nor read anything at all.

—So what if you don't write well? Like you said, you're not a novelist.

Perhaps this world truly was a novel called ‘Ways of Survival.’ Perhaps it was a story in a novel written by some author somewhere and read by someone.

But to her, this novel was life.

「And that gave her the right to write this world's next sentence.」

Slowly lowering her sword, Jung Heewon asked,

“······Dokja-ssi, you remember that time, don't you?”

She did not know whether Kim Dokja was listening. She simply placed her hand on the tiny scratch she had made on that vast wall. Through it flowed the scenes of places they had walked together. Two people in suits, climbing the stairs to heaven.

“I really liked that. Going to the department store together to buy clothes, then visiting <Eden> all dressed up.”

She liked this world. Everything was falling apart, and all she could see were ruins. Even so, it was in a world like this that Jung Heewon had found her worth.

“······You said it yourself. That you liked this world better. That's the kind of people we are.”

Kim Dokja did not answer.

Jung Heewon widened the wound in the tentacle. As though asking him not to forget that wound. As though asking him to remember the part of her that was as large as that wound.

“So this is the only way you can do things. Isn't it?”

Jung Heewon understood Kim Dokja.

「If she did not kill Kim Dokja, this world would be destroyed.」

The enormous Outer God King's eyes watched her. Its head even seemed to move as though agreeing with her wishes. Looking into those eyes, Jung Heewon said,

“How could I kill you?”
